title: Nepal Makes Electronic Tracking Devices Mandatory for Everest Climbers
summary: Nepal's Department of Tourism made electronic tracking devices mandatory for all mountaineers attempting Mount Everest starting from the spring 2024 climbing season. Climbers are required to carry an electronic tracking device or avalanche rescue reflector (such as Recco technology or satellite beacon) on their person or climbing harness to accelerate search and rescue operations in the event of an avalanche or crevasse fall.
source: The Kathmandu Post / Nepal Department of Tourism
author: Kathmandu Post reporting

title: Kami Rita Sherpa Summits Everest for a Record 32nd Time
summary: The 56-year-old veteran Nepali mountain guide reached the summit of Mount Everest on May 17, 2026, extending his world record to 32 career ascents. Kami Rita first stood on the summit of Everest in 1994 and has dedicated over three decades to high-altitude guiding and route establishment on the world's highest peaks.
source: Nepal Department of Tourism / The Himalayan Database
author: Himalayan News Reporting

title: UIAA Mountain Medicine: Medical Advice & Recommendations
summary: The UIAA Medical Commission publishes consensus guidance for mountain medicine, covering high-altitude illness (AMS, HAPE, HACE), water disinfection, and expedition first-aid protocols. These clinical documents form the primary medical standards for high-altitude health and safety globally.
source: UIAA — International Climbing and Mountaineering Federation
author: UIAA Medical Commission

title: Accidents in North American Climbing (Annual Safety Publication)
summary: The American Alpine Club's annual review analyses climbing and mountaineering accidents by root cause — belay failures, rappel mistakes, anchor errors, and objective hazards — providing empirical data that guides safety education across the international mountaineering community.
author: AAC Safety Committee

title: The Himalayan Database: Expedition Archives of Nepal
summary: Founded by Elizabeth Hawley and curated by an independent research team, the Himalayan Database compiles comprehensive summit, route, and casualty records for all significant Nepalese expeditions. It remains the gold standard for verifying Himalayan ascent claims.
author: Himalayan Database Team

title: Sagarmatha Pollution Control Committee: Everest Waste Management
summary: The SPCC oversees waste management systems across Everest Base Camp and the Khumbu trekking corridors, partnering with the Nepal Army to recover discarded high-altitude equipment, empty oxygen canisters, and packaging from upper camps.
author: SPCC Environmental Management

title: IFMGA: International Mountain Guide Professional Standards
summary: The International Federation of Mountain Guides Associations establishes rigorous training and credentialing standards across its 27 member nations, certifying mountain guides in avalanche rescue, technical rock, ice, and high-altitude navigation.
author: IFMGA Technical Commission

title: Piolets d'Or: Promoting Ethical Alpine-Style Ascents
summary: The annual Piolets d'Or honors lightweight, self-reliant alpine-style ascents executed without fixed ropes, supplemental oxygen, or heavy siege support. The awards represent mountaineering's highest recognition for purity of style.
author: Piolets d'Or Jury
